input.quote: 14.3 Choice of Law; Arbitration; Venue. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA, excluding conflict of laws provisions and excluding the 1980 United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods. Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the then-current commercial arbitration rules of the American Arbitration Association ("RULES"). The arbitration shall be conducted by one (1) arbitrator appointed in accordance with the Rules in San Francisco County, California.
input.rationale: Section 14.3 selects California law, which is expressly within the accepted list, and seats dispute resolution in San Francisco County, California — a domestic US forum with award enforcement available in the California courts. This sits at the playbook fallback (California law and forum) rather than the preferred position (New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County), so it is acceptable and not redlined. Two sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording but are not material failures: disputes go to mandatory single-arbitrator AAA arbitration rather than directly to court, and the venue for enforcement is San Francisco rather than New York County. Neither triggers the walk-away test, which is limited to a vendor home jurisdiction outside the accepted list with exclusive foreign venue or arbitration seated abroad; the seat here is domestic and California is not an off-list jurisdiction. Section 12 (source code escrow) refers disputes back to Section 14.3, so the same accepted forum governs throughout, and no competing jurisdiction clause appears elsewhere in the Agreement.
